session_recap:
The major indices ended the session in the red across the board, though losses were modest and differentiated. The S&P 500 slipped 8.40 points (-0.12%) to close at 7,130.40, while the Dow Jones bore more pressure, falling 282.27 points (-0.57%) to 48,859.66. The Nasdaq showed remarkable resilience, shedding only 11.58 points (-0.05%) to 24,652.22, and the Russell 2000 declined 12.02 points (-0.44%) to 2,744.03. The divergence between the Dow's heavier losses and the Nasdaq's near-flatness signals a tale of two markets: mega-cap tech and semis held up while traditional economy names struggled. The VIX edged higher by 0.39 points (+2.19%) to 18.22, reflecting building anxiety ahead of tonight's four-way Magnificent 7 earnings event.

The dominant macro story was a sharp 5.40% surge in WTI crude oil to $105.33 — the single biggest macro move of the session. News tied the move to geopolitical developments around stalled U.S.–Iran peace talks and supply-side implications. Energy names rode that wave, with Phillips 66 (PSX) surging +5.88% to $174.84 after topping Q1 earnings estimates. Gold, counterintuitively, sold off -0.85% to $4,552.40 — suggesting the crude move is a supply-disruption story rather than a broad inflation trade. The 10-year Treasury yield rose +4.4 bps to 4.40%, adding modest headwinds for rate-sensitive equities.

Semiconductor names dominated the gainers list in a notable earnings-driven rotation. NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) vaulted +23.88% to $285.42 — the session's top single-stock move — after the company beat Q1 estimates on broad-based end demand (Zacks). Intel (INTC) gained +10.23% on 104.4M shares as AI infrastructure rotation themes gained momentum. Amphenol (APH) gained +5.51% after beating Q1 revenue and guiding higher on AI data center demand (Reuters). The clearest loser theme was the crypto-adjacent equity complex, triggered by Robinhood (HOOD) falling -13.70% after reporting a cryptocurrency revenue slump. Coinbase (COIN) dropped -7.61%, RIOT -6.94%, MARA -6.03%. GE HealthCare (GEHC) fell -13.20% after a profit miss and guidance cut.
crypto_recap:
Bitcoin held above the technically significant $76,000 level, gaining +0.25% to $76,210 on $36.9B in 24-hour volume — a modest positive given the pressure on crypto-equity names from the Robinhood miss. Ethereum fared slightly better at +0.54% to $2,286.41 on $15.9B in volume. XRP slipped -0.46% to $1.37 on selling pressure ahead of the FOMC, with 99Bitcoins noting pressure building below $1.40. BNB fell -0.71% to $618.18.

The standout top-20 mover was Dogecoin (DOGE) at +6.31% to $0.11 on $3.5B in 24-hour volume — suggesting a discrete retail rotation into higher-beta tokens. ZEC was the top loser among the top 20, falling -2.94% to $324.12. Tether (USDT) volume of $63.8B — well above BTC+ETH combined — reflects highly active stablecoin trading flows. The disconnect between broadly flat-to-positive spot prices and the -7% to -14% declines in crypto equities (HOOD, COIN, RIOT, MARA) points to skepticism about trading volume sustainability rather than spot demand.
today_setup:

After the close: GOOG/GOOGL (EPS est $2.64, $4.23T mkt cap) — AI search, cloud growth, and OpenAI competitive response are the watch items; MSFT (EPS est $4.07, $3.19T) — Azure growth rate and AI capex tone set the narrative for all cloud names; AMZN (EPS est $1.60, $2.79T) — AWS trajectory and tariff impact on retail margins; META (EPS est $6.71, $1.70T) — Reels ad revenue and AI capex discipline. Also after hours: KLAC (EPS est $9.16) in semi equipment — yesterday's NXPI/APH beats set a favorable bar; QCOM (EPS est $1.90) on mobile handset recovery and AI-on-device; Ford ($0.20) on EV economics and tariff pass-through; Chipotle ($0.24) on consumer traffic and pricing power.

Pre-market already reported: ADP beat +5.85%, PSX beat +5.88%, APH beat +5.51%, REGN beat but sold off -5.86%, GEHC missed badly -13.20%, SOFI mixed -12.80%.

The pipeline returned no scheduled economic events today. However, multiple news sources reference 'Fed Chair Powell's final policy decision' — watch for the FOMC announcement and press conference. Any language on the rate path, Fed independence, or succession would be an outsized market event that will frame tonight's earnings interpretation.

crypto_outlook:
For the next 24 hours, the crypto complex is caught between two crosscurrents. On the bullish side, BTC's hold above $76,000 carries technical significance — Barron's framed the question as whether BTC is breaking out or topping, and a sustained close above $76,500 would favor the former. ETH's +0.54% session slightly outperforming BTC's +0.25% suggests modest alt rotation beginning. DOGE's +6.31% move on $3.5B volume is consistent with risk-on behavior within the asset class. Visa's stablecoin settlement expansion to Base, Polygon, Canton, Arc, and Tempo is a quiet institutional adoption signal.

The primary near-term risk is the FOMC decision. XRP's slide below $1.40 and multiple news headlines explicitly cited the rate decision as a headwind. If Powell signals higher-for-longer, BTC may retest $74K support. A hold or dovish tone would likely clear the path for a relief rally back toward $78–80K. The crypto equity complex (HOOD, COIN, RIOT, MARA) will remain structurally under pressure until Robinhood's crypto revenue miss is contextualized away from spot market volumes.
risk_notes: Magnificent 4 earnings gauntlet (AH tonight): GOOG, MSFT, AMZN, META — ~$11.9T combined market cap. A collective miss or cautious AI-spend guide could gap the S&P 500 down 1.5–2%+ at tomorrow's open. Single largest event risk of the quarter.
WTI crude at $105.33 (+5.40% single session): If crude holds or extends, stagflation risk re-enters the macro narrative for consumer companies reporting over the next two weeks.

FOMC / Powell final policy decision: Any surprise on rates, tone regarding Fed independence, or succession uncertainty would be an outsized volatility event across rates, USD, and risk assets — and will frame how the market interprets tonight's earnings.
